title: Cocontinuous natural transformations on modules are detected on the ring
statement: Let R be a commutative ring in universe u, D a category, and F,G:ModuleCat.{u} R → D functors preserving colimits of size (u,u). Let alpha:F → G be a natural transformation. If alpha at the rank-one free module R is an isomorphism, then alpha at every R-module M is an isomorphism. No additive structure on D or additivity of the functors is assumed.

source.place: PresheafOfModules.isIso_app_of_freeYoneda: coproduct and cokernel argument, specialized to ordinary modules

proof.text: For a type I, construct the cofan from copies of R to the free module R^(I), with inclusion at i sending 1 to its basis vector. A map out of this cofan is uniquely the linear extension of the images of those basis vectors. Thus this cofan is colimiting. Since F and G preserve these coproducts, naturality and invertibility of alpha_R imply invertibility of alpha on R^(I).

For a module M let g:R^(M) → M send [m] to m, and let f:R^(ker g) → R^(M) send [x] to x. The map g is surjective and im f = ker g: each kernel element x is the image of the basis vector [x], and g(f([x]))=0 extends linearly. Hence g exhibits M as the cokernel of f, equivalently the coequalizer of f and zero.

Both F and G preserve that coequalizer. The transformation between the two image diagrams is an isomorphism at both free vertices by step 1. The induced map between their colimits, which is alpha_M by naturality, is therefore an isomorphism.
